problem: Prior VLN/ALFRED agents are recurrent (LSTM). They keep history only in a hidden state and fail on long compositional episodes: ALFRED tasks average 50 steps and 6.5 subgoals, with object interactions. They also struggle to ground highly variable human instructions, and the gap is largest in unseen environments.
motivation: Long household tasks require recalling things seen much earlier (e.g. a fireplace at t=0 reused at t=31) and resolving coreferences such as 'where you were standing previously'. Recurrent state is poor at such long-term dependencies. Separately, task specifications like PDDL subgoals state the goal without depending on visual appearance or human phrasing variation. The authors hypothesize that such 'synthetic instructions' can serve as an intermediate representation that makes learning easier and generalize better.
key_idea: Replace the recurrent policy with a causal multimodal transformer that attends over the instruction, the full episode of visual frames and past actions. Then use PDDL-derived synthetic subgoal instructions both to pretrain the language encoder (human→synthetic translation) and as extra jointly-trained demonstrations.
insight:
Full-episode visual memory is what matters. With subgoal-level (short-horizon) success, LSTM and E.T. are close (75.5 vs 77.3 seen), but full-task success jumps from 23.2 to 33.8 (Table 1). Accessible visual history scales monotonically (0.5 with no frames → 28.9 with 1 frame → 33.8 with all). Action history does the opposite: 1 past action is best (33.8) and all actions drops to 27.1, attributed to causal misidentification. Synthetic language helps most in abstract, task-oriented form:
- Subgoal-action annotations for joint training beat speaker-generated text and expert-frame goals on human instructions (38.5/5.4 vs 37.4/3.9 vs 28.5/3.4 val seen/unseen).
- Transferring the seq2seq-pretrained encoder weights beats explicit translation (37.6 vs 35.2) and generic BERT (32.3).
- Pretraining and joint training are complementary (46.6/7.3), with the biggest relative gain in unseen scenes.
- E.T. benefits 2.3–4.4× more from the extra data than an LSTM does.
- Capacity matters: 2 transformer blocks is the sweet spot; 4 blocks overfits (19.8 seen).
- Gains from synthetic data saturate around 22K demos.
method: Episodic Transformer policy: language encoder (lookup table + 2-block transformer, 768-d, 12 heads) produces contextualized word embeddings, and a multimodal 2-block transformer encoder with causal attention takes [language tokens; visual embeddings v_1:t; action embeddings] with sinusoidal positional/temporal encodings. A single FC layer on the visual output tokens predicts the action (13 types) and the target object class (119 classes).

Visual encoder: frozen ResNet-50 backbone pretrained as Faster R-CNN on 325K ALFRED train frames. Features are avg-pooled to 512×7×7, passed through 2 1×1 convs (256, 64) and an FC to a 768-d per-frame embedding. Each frame is encoded independently, and all frames of the episode are kept as memory.

Interaction masks: following MOCA, the predicted target class retrieves an instance mask from a frozen pretrained Mask R-CNN (300×300 input). MOCA's Instance Association in Time and Obstruction Detection modules are used at evaluation.

Training: teacher-forced, predicting all T actions of an expert demo in one forward pass with cross-entropy, plus 0.1-weighted auxiliary overall/subgoal progress losses. AdamW (wd 0.33), lr 1e-4 then 1e-5, 20 epochs × 3,750 batches of 8. At test the last-step prediction is executed. Only the last previous action is fed (visual history unlimited).
Synthetic language: each expert demo is annotated with its PDDL subgoal sequence (e.g. 'Goto Bed', 'Put Apple Table'), giving class-level, instance-free instructions.

Language encoder pretraining: a transformer seq2seq model (same encoder architecture, decoder of the same size) translates human instructions to synthetic ones on the train fold, reaching 97.1 F1. Its encoder weights initialize the agent's language encoder.

Joint training: 44,996 extra AI2-THOR demos (new object configurations and start poses in train scenes) are annotated with synthetic instructions. Each batch mixes 4 human and 4 synthetic demos, with a shared encoder but separate token lookup tables for the two vocabularies.

setting.backbone: Frozen ResNet-50 (Faster R-CNN-pretrained on ALFRED frames) + 2-block transformer language & multimodal encoders trained from scratch; frozen Mask R-CNN (from MOCA) for interaction masks
setting.training_data: ALFRED train fold (21,023 human annotations over 8,055 expert trajectories). Language encoder pretrained on human→synthetic (PDDL subgoal) translation pairs from the train fold. Joint training adds 44,996 synthetic-instruction demonstrations generated in AI2-THOR train environments. Visual encoder / Mask R-CNN pretrained on 325K train frames with segmentation masks.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (224×224 for policy, 300×300 for mask generator) + natural-language goal/step instructions + previous action
setting.action_space: 13 discrete action types (navigation moves/turns/look + 7 object interactions) plus predicted target object class mapped to a Mask R-CNN instance mask
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT masks and PDDL subgoals used only for training / synthetic data generation)

numbers_note: The ALFRED test-seen fold is recorded as split 'test' (with 'TEST-SEEN fold' in extra) because the allowed split vocabulary has no test-seen value. GC = goal-condition success. PLW-SR / PLW-GC are the path-length-weighted scores printed in parentheses in Table A1. Ablation tables (history length, capacity, synthetic-instruction types, data size) report val SR only and are summarized in insight rather than listed.
results:
The full model E.T. (pretr. & joint tr.) set a new ALFRED state of the art at submission time.
- Test: 38.42 SR seen / 8.57 SR unseen, vs MOCA's 22.05 / 5.30.
- Validation: 46.59 / 7.32 vs MOCA's 19.15 / 3.78.

Plain E.T. already beats MOCA on seen (28.77 test) but not on test unseen (5.04 vs 5.30). Synthetic-language pretraining plus joint training brings a +37.8% relative gain on val seen and +228.1% on val unseen over plain E.T.
limitations: Generalization to unseen environments remains very weak: 8.57% test-unseen SR vs 91% human. Navigation failures and wrong-object pickups are the common failure modes.
Synthetic instructions depend on ALFRED's PDDL expert planner and the ability to generate new demos in simulation, and the 45K extra demos come from the train scenes. Gains saturate around 22K demos.
Transformer capacity must be kept small (2 blocks) to avoid overfitting. The agent also relies on MOCA's pretrained Mask R-CNN and inference heuristics (instance association, obstruction detection).
compares_to: LSTM baseline with same visual features
